title: [YouPass Collect] - Number of people affected by noise pollution in urban and rural areas: 2007
prompt: The charts below show the number of people in Europe who were affected by four types of noise by day and by night in cities and rural areas in 2007. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The two bar charts compare the number of Europeans who experienced noise pollution from four different sources, namely traffic, trains, aircraft, and industry, during the day and at night in urban and rural settings in 2007.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, traffic noise affected the largest number of people in both areas, while industrial noise had the least impact, with no recorded cases in the countryside. Additionally, daytime noise consistently disturbed more individuals than nighttime noise across all categories.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most significant noise sources, traffic was by far the dominant contributor in cities, affecting 64 million people during the day and 48 million at night. In rural areas, the corresponding figures were considerably lower, at 34 million and 24 million, respectively. Train noise ranked second, impacting 10 million and 8 million city dwellers during the day and night, while slightly fewer people in rural regions, approximately 8 million and 6 million, were affected.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for less significant sources, aircraft noise disturbed 4 million urban residents during the day, dropping to just 1 million at night, whereas the rural figures stood at 2 million and 1 million, in that order. Finally, industrial noise had a negligible effect, with only 1 million city inhabitants affected during the day and a mere 0.25 million at night. Notably, no one in rural areas reported being disturbed by this type of noise at any time of day.
